thread.title: Credit-card stocks cut more than 30 points from Dow industrials in early trade - MarketWatch

author: Mark DeCambre
title: Credit-card stocks cut more than 30 points from Dow industrials in early trade - MarketWatch
text:
Published: July 30, 2018 11:07 a.m. ET Share Mark DeCambre
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was struggling to retain a grip in positive territory early Monday, with the benchmark being yanked lower by a pair of credit-card components. Shares of American Express Co. AXP, -2.61% and VISA Inc. V, -2.88% were cutting more than 45 points from the price-weighted Dow DJIA, -0.38% in morning trade. The Dow was most recently trading off by 14 points, or less than 0.1%, at 25,436, with gains in Chevron Corp. CVX, +1.42% JPMorgan Chase & Co. JPM, +0.61% and McDonald's Corp. MCD, +0.80% trying to offset a slide by the credit-card companies. Meanwhile, a drop in technology shares weighed on the broader market, with the S&P 500 index SPX, -0.49% off 0.1% at 2,814 and the technology-focused Nasdaq Composite Index COMP, -1.27% sliding 0.7%, on the back of declines in Facebook Inc. FB, -3.18% Facebook's shares have fallen for three straight sessions after reporting quarterly results on July 25 that disappointed Wall Street, and prompted a reassessment of so-called FAANG stocks, including Google-parent Alphabet Inc. GOOG, -1.32% GOOGL, -1.62% Netflix Inc., NFLX, -5.33% and Apple Inc. AAPL, -0.63%
